_about: Which side of a dedicated-server setup each mod belongs on, so deploy-dathost.ps1 only
uploads what can actually run there and mod-status.ps1 stops reporting a client-only mod as
client  - never upload. The server has no use for it.
server  - upload; the server needs it and clients do not.
both    - upload, and clients need it too.
The authority for 'client' is usually the code itself: [BepInProcess("valheim.exe")] on the
plugin class makes BepInEx skip the plugin entirely under valheim_server.exe, so such a DLL
cannot run on the server no matter where it is copied. mod-status.ps1 cross-checks this file
against that attribute and reports any mod whose declared side contradicts its own code.
'profilePackages' covers the third-party packages mirrored by deploy-dathost.ps1 -Profile,
keyed by the package folder name as it appears in the Gale profile's BepInEx/plugins. Only
list one when it should be skipped or forced; anything absent is mirrored as before.

Armory.why: [BepInProcess("valheim.exe")] - cannot load on the dedicated server.

DudeWhatAreMyStats.why: No process gate, but stats are answered per-client over a routed RPC; README: 'the server needs nothing'.

ForsakenShrines.why: UNRESOLVED: [BepInProcess("valheim.exe")] says client-only, but thunderstore.toml lists the server-side category. The code wins here because the attribute is what BepInEx enforces, so the server copy was dead weight. If custom pieces do need a server install, the attribute is the bug, not this line.

GrabMaterials.why: [BepInProcess("valheim.exe")] - reads and moves the local player's inventory.

PauseMyServer.why: Server-authoritative: the server decides whether a pause is granted and broadcasts it; the client freezes.

TheGreatestMap.why: The shared marker store and the live portal list come from the server, and deploy-dathost.ps1's pre-stop world save depends on this mod's save-now trigger running there.

TheGreatestPortal.why: README: install on the server and on every client.
